title: Purchase tags fire once, only on the real purchase
pass: Every purchase and conversion tag fires on the dataLayer purchase event only, sends transaction_id, and has no extra trigger (no thank-you URL page view, no All Pages trigger, no trigger group missing a condition).
fails: A purchase tag fires on a thank-you page URL, so reloading or revisiting that page counts the order again; or a conversion tag is tied to a broad trigger and fires on unrelated pages.
validate: GTM read: for each purchase/conversion tag, list its firing triggers; fail if any is a page-view trigger with a thank-you/order URL filter, an All Pages trigger, or a trigger group without the purchase event condition; fail if transaction_id is not sent.
action: Have your developer fire purchase tags only on the purchase event and send the order number with it.
done_when: Every purchase tag in GTM has one trigger on the purchase event and sends transaction_id.
why_it_matters: Double-counted orders make your sales and conversion rate look higher than the money in your bank.
selected_because: An inflated order count makes every money number in the report untrustworthy for the owner.

title: Shopify checkout and orders are tracked
pass: The store is not on Shopify, or begin_checkout and purchase come from a Shopify Customer Events pixel or the native Google and YouTube integration.
fails: A Shopify store relies on GTM tags for checkout and purchase, but GTM does not run inside Shopify checkout, so those steps are missing or partial.
validate: Platform from the crawl and headless visit; GTM read for begin_checkout and purchase tags and their triggers; headless visit for the Shopify web-pixels / Customer Events sandbox scripts. Fail on Shopify when checkout/purchase depend on GTM tags only.
action: On Shopify, have your developer send checkout and purchase from a custom pixel in Settings > Customer events, or the native Google integration.
done_when: Checkout and purchase events come from a Customer Events pixel or the native integration, not from GTM tags alone.
why_it_matters: If checkout and orders are not recorded, GA4 cannot show your real sales or where shoppers drop out of checkout.
selected_because: A common Shopify gap that removes the last and most valuable funnel steps.

title: Consent settings do not hide your Gulf visitors
pass: Consent defaults are set per region, or the consent banner applies only where required, so visits from GCC markets are recorded normally.
fails: All tags are denied by default for every region, including markets with no such requirement, so many visits and sales are never recorded.
validate: GTM read: consent default tag parameters (region list, ad_storage, analytics_storage); headless visit without clicking the banner: decode the gcs/gcd parameter on GA4 hits to see whether storage is denied.
action: Have your developer set consent defaults per region so visitors in your markets are counted.
done_when: Consent default lists the regions that need it, and our visit from a GCC location sends GA4 hits with storage granted.
why_it_matters: Visits and orders blocked by consent disappear from your reports, so your sales look lower than they are.
selected_because: An over-strict banner removes real GCC sales from the owner's numbers.

title: Add to cart is counted once in tracking for each real add
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Our real Add-to-Cart click on a product page produced one add_to_cart event, including from a cart drawer or quick add.
fails: Add to cart fires only on a form submit or page change, so drawer and quick adds are not counted; or it fires on the click even when nothing was added.
validate: Headless phone visit: click Add to Cart on one product, confirm the cart count changed, and check the dataLayer and network for exactly one add_to_cart hit; GTM read for the add_to_cart trigger type.
action: Have your developer trigger add to cart from your theme's own add-to-cart event, not from a click or a page change.
done_when: A test add to cart on phone produces one add_to_cart event and the cart shows the item.
why_it_matters: A wrong add-to-cart count hides whether your product pages or your cart are losing the sale.
selected_because: Directly measured on the live store; decides which page the owner fixes first.

title: Each ad pixel is installed once, not twice
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Each ad pixel (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, Google) loads from one source only: a store app, GTM, or code, not two or three at once.
fails: The same pixel is added by a Salla, Zid or Shopify app and again through GTM or pasted code, so page views, add to carts and purchases are sent twice.
validate: Headless visit of home, product and cart: count base-pixel loads and event hits per pixel ID in the network log; compare with pixel tags in the GTM read. Fail if one pixel ID loads from more than one source or sends duplicate events for one action.
action: Pick one way to install each pixel (the store's app or GTM) and remove the other; you can switch off the app integration yourself, the GTM tag needs your developer.
done_when: Our re-scan sees each pixel ID load once and send one event per action.
why_it_matters: Double-sent sales make your ads look better than they are, so you may spend more on ads that do not sell.
selected_because: Tested in audits, failed on 2 of 3 stores; the owner can fix part of it in the admin.

title: Purchase tag set up for every ad platform you pay for
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Every paid channel that brings traffic (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok) has a purchase event tag in GTM with an active purchase trigger, or its purchases come from the store-app integration.
fails: GA4 shows paid traffic from Snapchat, TikTok or Meta, but GTM has no purchase tag for that platform and no store-app integration sends it.
validate: GA4 report: paid channels by source; GTM read: for each paying platform, a purchase event tag with an active purchase trigger. Live pixel loading and page-view/add-to-cart firing is checked in the website section, not here.
action: Have your developer add a purchase event for the missing platform's pixel.
done_when: Each platform sending paid visits has a purchase tag with an active trigger in GTM, or a store-app integration that sends purchases.
why_it_matters: An ad platform that never sees your sales cannot find more buyers like them.
selected_because: Ties tracking to ad money the owner already spends.

title: WhatsApp and call clicks are counted
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Clicks on WhatsApp and phone links fire an event, or the store has no such links.
fails: The store shows a WhatsApp or call button but no tag records the click, so orders that start in WhatsApp are invisible.
validate: Headless visit lists wa.me, api.whatsapp.com and tel: links; GTM read for link-click triggers on those URLs and the event they send. Fail if links exist and no tag tracks them.
action: Have your developer track WhatsApp and call button clicks as an event in GTM.
done_when: A click on the WhatsApp button sends an event, visible in our re-scan.
why_it_matters: Shoppers who order through WhatsApp look like lost visitors, so you cannot see which pages and ads bring them.
selected_because: WhatsApp is a main sales channel for GCC stores and is usually untracked.

title: Your data goes to your own GA4 only
pass: Every GA4 tag uses one constant variable holding the store's own measurement ID.
fails: Old or hard-coded IDs send visits and sales to another GA4 property, such as one from a past agency.
validate: GTM read: collect every G- ID in tags and variables; headless visit: list G- IDs in GA4 hits. Fail if any ID is not the store's connected property.
action: Have your developer keep one GA4 ID in one variable and remove the others.
done_when: Only your own GA4 ID appears in GTM and in our visit.
why_it_matters: Sales sent to another property are missing from your reports, and someone else can see your sales.
selected_because: Split data hides part of the owner's sales.

title: Ad pixel loads before its events
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Each pixel's base tag loads before its event tags (by tag sequencing or priority), so add-to-cart and purchase events are received.
fails: Event tags fire before the base pixel is ready, so some add-to-cart or purchase events are lost.
validate: GTM read: setup-tag sequencing and firing priority on pixel event tags; headless visit: order of base-pixel load and event hits in the network log.
action: Have your developer set each pixel's base tag to load before its event tags.
done_when: Every pixel event tag has the base tag as its setup tag, and our visit sees the base load first.
why_it_matters: Lost events mean your ad platforms see fewer sales than you made.
selected_because: Tested in audits, failed on 2 of 3 stores; causes sales to go missing in ad platforms.

title: Meta does not count the same sale twice
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: The Meta Purchase event fires with an event_id that can match a server event, or Meta is not used.
fails: The Meta pixel is present without a Purchase event, or without an event_id, so Meta cannot match browser and server sales.
validate: GTM read: Meta pixel tags (Custom HTML or template) and their event name and eventID parameters; headless visit: event_id present on Meta hits we can trigger (view content, add to cart).
action: Have your developer send Purchase to Meta with an order-based event_id, and use the same id in the Conversions API if you use it.
done_when: The Meta Purchase tag in GTM sends an event_id.
why_it_matters: Without a matching id Meta can count one sale twice or miss it, so you cannot trust Meta's sales number.
selected_because: Meta is the main paid channel for GCC stores.

title: Each ad platform gets your sales on one pixel ID
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Each ad platform (Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, Google Ads) uses one pixel or conversion ID, kept in one constant variable that all its tags read.
fails: Two different pixel IDs for the same platform fire together, or one platform's tags use different hard-coded IDs, so your sales are split across pixels and each sees only part of them.
validate: GTM read: collect pixel and conversion IDs from every Meta, Snapchat, TikTok and Google Ads tag and variable; group by platform; fail if a platform has more than one active ID or IDs are typed into tags instead of read from one variable.
action: Confirm with whoever runs your ads which pixel ID is yours, and have your developer use only that one, from one variable.
done_when: Each platform has one ID in GTM, read from one variable.
why_it_matters: When sales are split across two pixels, each ad account sees fewer sales than you made and spends less well.
selected_because: Backfill: next most valuable measurable GTM candidate; covers ad pixel IDs (SO-GTM-08 covers the GA4 ID only).

title: Google Ads sees your sales
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: When Google Ads traffic exists, a Google Ads conversion tag and the Conversion Linker are present (or GA4 conversions are imported), with enhanced conversions on.
fails: GA4 shows Google Ads traffic but there is no conversion tag or linker, or enhanced conversions are off.
validate: GA4 report: google / cpc sessions; GTM read: awct and Conversion Linker tags and the enhanced conversions setting on the tag.
action: Have your developer add the Google Ads purchase tag and the Conversion Linker, with enhanced conversions.
done_when: GTM has a Google Ads purchase tag and Conversion Linker, both with active triggers.
why_it_matters: Google Ads can only find more buyers if it sees which clicks became sales.
selected_because: Relevant when the owner pays for Google Ads, shown only then.

title: Key tags fire on store events, not on how buttons look
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Tags for checkout, WhatsApp, sign-up and other key actions fire on dataLayer events or link addresses, not on CSS classes, element IDs or button text.
fails: Triggers depend on CSS classes, element IDs or button text, so a theme update or redesign stops them firing without anyone noticing.
validate: GTM read: for each active tag on a shopping or contact action (add to cart has its own point), list trigger types and conditions; flag Click or Element Visibility triggers matching on Click Classes, Click ID, CSS selectors or Click Text.
action: Have your developer switch these triggers to the store's own events so they keep working after theme changes.
done_when: No key-action tag in GTM relies on a CSS class, element ID or button text.
why_it_matters: Tags tied to how a button looks stop counting the day you change or update your theme.
selected_because: Backfill: theme changes are common on Salla, Zid and Shopify stores; fully readable from the container.

title: Newsletter and contact form sign-ups are counted
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: When the store has an email, phone or WhatsApp sign-up form, one tag sends sign_up or generate_lead when the form is sent successfully.
fails: The store collects emails or phone numbers and no tag records it, or the tag fires on every submit click (including failed ones), or two tags count the same form.
validate: Crawl and headless visit list sign-up and contact forms on home, product and footer (we do not submit them); GTM read: tags sending sign_up, generate_lead or form events, their triggers (form submit with a success check, or a dataLayer event) and duplicate tags for the same form.
action: Have your developer send a sign-up event when a customer leaves an email or number on your store.
done_when: GTM has one active sign-up tag per form, firing only on a successful submit.
why_it_matters: You can only grow your WhatsApp and email list if you see which pages and ads bring sign-ups.
selected_because: Backfill: current-tool point merged with form tracking (same check); ties to the owner's WhatsApp and email list.

title: Ad click IDs are saved so ad platforms can match sales
group_en: Your ad platforms see your real sales
pass: Ad click IDs (gclid, fbclid, ttclid, ScCid) are stored when a shopper lands from an ad.
fails: Paid visitors arrive with click IDs and nothing stores them, so the sale cannot be tied back to the ad.
validate: Headless visit to a product page with test gclid, fbclid and ttclid parameters added to the URL; check first-party cookies (_gcl_aw, _fbc, _ttp or similar) after load; GTM read for the Conversion Linker and URL-parameter variables.
action: Have your developer add the Conversion Linker and store ad click IDs in first-party cookies.
done_when: Our test visit with click IDs leaves matching first-party cookies.
why_it_matters: When the click is not stored, sales show up as unknown, and you cannot tell which ads sell.
selected_because: Lets the owner see which ads bring sales.

title: Ad and analytics tags don't send plain customer emails or phone numbers
pass: No raw email, phone or name in tag parameters or in the dataLayer variables tags read; any customer data a platform asks for is hashed and sent only with consent.
fails: Email or phone is sent as plain text in a tag parameter, often in hand-built pixel advanced matching.
validate: GTM read: scan tag parameters and dataLayer variables used by tags for email or phone fields and hashing settings. Personal data in page addresses is checked in GA4, not here.
action: Have your developer remove plain customer details from tags and URLs, or hash them where the platform requires it.
done_when: No plain email or phone appears in any GTM tag parameter.
why_it_matters: Sending customer details in plain text puts your customers' trust and your accounts at risk.
selected_because: A real risk the owner is responsible for, kept as one merged privacy point.

title: Your latest tracking fixes are actually live
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: The container version the live store loads is the latest published version, and no finished changes sit unpublished in the workspace.
fails: The live site loads an older container version, or fixes sit in the workspace and were never published, so the store still runs the old tracking.
validate: GTM read: latest published version number and date, and workspace status (pending changes); crawl: fetch the live gtm.js for the container and read its version; fail if they differ or the workspace has pending tag, trigger or variable changes.
action: Ask your developer to publish finished changes and confirm the live store loads the new version.
done_when: The live gtm.js version equals the latest published version and the workspace has no pending changes.
why_it_matters: A fix that was never published never reaches your reports.
selected_because: Backfill: measurable from the container read plus one crawl; catches fixes that never went live.

title: No unknown scripts running on your store
pass: Every Custom HTML tag has a known purpose and owner, and official tag templates are used where they exist.
fails: Custom HTML tags load scripts from unknown vendors, or hand-pasted pixel code is used where an official template exists and breaks without notice.
validate: GTM read: list Custom HTML tags, the domains their scripts load, and whether an official template exists for that vendor; headless visit: domains loaded by GTM.
action: Have your developer remove scripts no one recognises and switch hand-pasted pixels to official templates.
done_when: Every Custom HTML tag in GTM has a named purpose, and known pixels use official templates.
why_it_matters: Unknown scripts can break your pages or collect your customers' data without you knowing.
selected_because: A risk the owner can ask about and verify.

title: Pages that change without reloading are still counted
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: If the store changes pages without a full reload, a page view fires on each change and old product data is cleared; or the store reloads on every page.
fails: The store changes pages without reloading, but GTM fires only on the first load, so later pages and products viewed are not counted.
validate: Headless visit: move from home to collection to product by tapping links and note whether the document reloads or the address changes by script; when it changes by script, check for one page_view per change; GTM read for History Change triggers and ecommerce clearing.
action: Have your developer add page-change triggers in GTM if your store loads pages without reloading.
done_when: Each page change in our visit sends one page view.
why_it_matters: Pages and products that are not counted vanish from your funnel and product reports.
selected_because: Backfill: two candidates measuring the same history-change setup merged; only applies to stores that load pages by script.

title: Old agency and campaign tags removed
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: No paused tags, tags with no trigger, or pixels from past vendors and ended campaigns.
fails: Tags from a past agency or old campaigns still load on every visit, slowing pages and sending your data to vendors you no longer use.
validate: GTM read: paused flag, tags without firing triggers, vendor names and IDs not matching current platforms; headless visit: requests to those vendors.
action: Have your developer delete dead and past-vendor tags.
done_when: GTM has no paused, trigger-less or past-vendor tags.
why_it_matters: Old tags slow your store and keep sending your data to people you stopped working with.
selected_because: Easy cleanup with a speed and data-risk effect the owner understands.

title: Your team's visits are kept out of sales numbers
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: A traffic_type parameter, IP rule or logged-in-staff exception marks your team's own visits.
fails: Nothing marks the team's visits, so your own browsing and test orders mix with real customers.
validate: GTM read: traffic_type parameter on the Google tag, or a blocking exception for staff or admin sessions.
action: Have your developer mark your team's visits so GA4 can leave them out.
done_when: The Google tag sends traffic_type for team visits, or staff sessions are blocked.
why_it_matters: Your own visits make conversion rate and product views look different from what customers do.
selected_because: Small, clean fix that makes the owner's numbers truer.

title: Triggers don't depend on switched-off settings
group_en: Tags that fit your store and keep it fast
group_ar: أكواد التتبع تناسب متجرك وما تبطّئه
pass: Every built-in variable a trigger or tag uses (Page URL, Click URL, Click Text, Form ID and so on) is turned on in the container.
fails: A trigger uses a built-in variable that is turned off, so its tag never fires as intended.
validate: GTM read: list enabled built-in variables and every {{variable}} reference in triggers and tags; fail on references to built-ins that are not enabled.
action: Have your developer turn on the built-in variables your triggers use.
done_when: No trigger or tag references a disabled built-in variable.
why_it_matters: A tag that silently never fires is a step or sale you never see.
selected_because: Backfill: fully readable from the container; low value but it decides whether tags fire.

title: Consent banner works before and after the choice
pass: Where a consent banner is used, the consent default fires on Consent Initialization before any tag, and marketing tags require ad_storage consent.
fails: The consent default is missing or loads late, or pixels fire with no consent check, so the banner has no real effect.
validate: GTM read: consent tag trigger (Consent Initialization - All Pages) and each marketing tag's consent settings; headless visit: whether pixel hits are sent before any banner choice.
action: Have your developer load consent defaults first and link marketing tags to consent.
done_when: Consent default runs on Consent Initialization and each marketing tag lists its consent requirement.
why_it_matters: A banner that does not work exposes you to complaints from customers in regions that require consent.
selected_because: Kept as one low point; matters mainly for stores selling outside the GCC.

title: Session recordings installed to check your fixes
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Microsoft Clarity or Hotjar is installed and its script actually loads on the live store.
fails: No recording tool, or a tag set up in GTM that never loads on the live site.
validate: GTM read for Clarity or Hotjar tags; crawl and headless visit for their script requests on live pages. We only check that it loads; we do not read its data.
action: Install Microsoft Clarity (free) through GTM or your store's app so you can watch how shoppers use the pages you fix.
done_when: Our re-scan sees the recording script load on home and product pages.
why_it_matters: Recordings let you see whether a fix helped shoppers, not just guess.
selected_because: Tested in audits, failed on 3 of 4 stores; helps the owner confirm fixes.

title: Visits to missing pages are recorded
group_ar: شوف وين يطلع العميل قبل الشراء
pass: Visits to a not-found page send an event (or a page title GA4 can filter) with the page address and where the visitor came from.
fails: Not-found visits look like normal page views, so dead links in ads, posts and messages go unseen.
validate: Headless visit to a made-up address on the store: check whether a page_view with a not-found title or a dedicated error event is sent; GTM read for a 404 trigger or tag.
action: Have your developer send a not-found event with the page address and referrer.
done_when: Our visit to a missing page sends a not-found event.
why_it_matters: Ads and WhatsApp links that land on a missing page lose the sale; tracking them shows which links to fix.
selected_because: Backfill: measurable in one headless visit; pairs with the website section's dead-link check without measuring the same thing.
